about: SDG links for the nine roles and their ESCO skills. Roles: one or two targets each, with the reason tied to the role's own ESCO essential skills. Skills: rules in src/sdg.ts using ESCO's green and digital flags and the skill's wording; every skill also counts towards target 4.4 (relevant skills for decent jobs). Target wording is shortened from the UN 2030 Agenda. Drafted 21 Oct 2026; review status in 'review'.
review: Drafted with Claude on 21 Oct 2026 from the ESCO skills listed; to be reviewed by the team before submission.

billing-clerk.reason: Clerical accounting work is among the most exposed to generative AI in the ILO index. Helping people move from it into more resilient work is what full and productive employment asks for.

accounting-assistant.reason: Clerical accounting work is among the most exposed to generative AI in the ILO index. Helping people move from it into more resilient work is what full and productive employment asks for.

bookkeeper.reason: Routine bookkeeping is highly exposed to generative AI. Keeping bookkeepers in productive work as tasks change supports decent work for all.

accountant.reason: Its essential skills include ensuring compliance with accounting conventions and explaining accounting records: reliable accounts make organisations accountable and transparent.
Fraud detection is one of its essential skills.

financial-analyst.reason: Its essential skills include advising on financial matters and offering financial services.

business-analyst.reason: Its essential skills include advising on efficiency improvements and analysing business plans: raising productivity through better processes.

data-analyst.reason: Its essential skills include defining data quality criteria and implementing data quality processes.
Analysing big data and data mining build an organisation’s research and technological capability.

software-developer.reason: Building and debugging software upgrades the technological capabilities of the organisations it serves.

sustainability-manager.reason: It leads the sustainability reporting process and measures the company’s sustainability performance (essential skills).
It advises on carbon emissions reduction and assesses climate change impact (essential skills).
